column1: # WHAT THE ENABLE-LATCH BYPASS FIX CHANGES, measured over every retained block
# A (before) = this worktree with the per-port MEMORY GATE FOLD present and the
#              enable-latch bypass UNCHANGED (it tested the raw `And` operand
#              for Ntype_op::Latch, so it never fired through the width wrapper
#              both readers put between a latch output and the gate).
# Each block: `lhd pass single_edge` on its RETAINED lgdb_raw, then cgen
# Verilog from the result; the sha256 is of that Verilog. FRONT END ONLY -- no
# certificate, no Lean, no corpus run, and nothing here rewrites a recorded
# table. The emission was first checked to be DETERMINISTIC (same binary twice,
# three blocks, identical hashes), so a hash difference is a real difference.
# RESULT: acceptance never changed and no refusal code changed. Eleven blocks'
# normalized emission changed, every one in the same way -- a gated endpoint's
# enable moved from the ICG latch's HELD Q to the value that latch passes
# through at the sampling edge. Nine of those eleven are blocks the historical
# tables already record as accepted; their recorded emissions predate this fix.
